layer1_philosophy.methodology: A bilingual Grade 1 literacy system with language-specific foundational reading instruction, a content-rich reader's workshop, and repeated oral reading through Reader's Theater. English phonics follows an explicit systematic sound-spelling progression. Spanish foundational literacy follows the traditional Spanish progression from vowels and consonants through syllables, words, closed syllables, clusters, diphthongs, hiatuses, stress, and morphology.
principles: Teach English and Spanish foundational literacy as distinct language systems. Do not translate English phonics order into Spanish.
Make sound-spelling instruction explicit, cumulative, and connected to reading and writing every day.
Use a gradual sequence in Spanish: vowels, consonants, syllables, words, closed syllables, clusters, diphthongs, hiatuses, stress, and word parts.
Move from brief whole-group modeling into shared, guided, independent, and reflective reading within a 50 to 60 minute reader's workshop.
Revisit texts for a new purpose, then transfer the reading move into independent reading and response.
Use daily observation and cumulative assessment to adjust instruction while keeping the result descriptive rather than a verdict on a child.
Build oral reading fluency through meaningful repeated rehearsal, performance, and self-reflection.

layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: Explicit language-specific modeling, cumulative practice, connected reading and writing, gradual release, text rereading for changing purposes, independent transfer, formative observation, and meaningful repeated oral reading.
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: Use daily response and observation, spelling and dictation evidence, weekly pattern work, cumulative phonics assessment, conference notes, comprehension checks, performance rehearsal, and self-reflection. Code verifies any exact scoring or progression rule; the parent uses the evidence to choose support.
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: Act as teacher, reading partner, and observer. Model the day's sound-spelling or comprehension move, practice together, choose accessible connected texts, listen during independent use, record what the child actually does, and adjust pacing or support. Classroom groups become parent-child, sibling, or invited-peer turns without changing the source's instructional purpose.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark Grade 1 bilingual reading workshop format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A Grade 1 format combining parallel 30-week English and Spanish foundational-literacy progressions, 135 captured reader's-workshop minilessons, and ten five-day Reader's Theater sequences.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Run the English and Spanish foundational-literacy lanes as separate language systems over ten units and 30 weeks, with five daily blocks per week. Pair explicit sound-spelling or syllable work with shared reading, connected text, writing, reflection, and cumulative assessment. Use the captured reader's-workshop minilessons within a 50 to 60 minute block that moves from a whole-group model to small-group or independent reading and response. Add ten five-day Reader's Theater cycles: introduce and discuss the script, model fluent reading, assign and analyze roles, rehearse with feedback, perform, and self-reflect. In a homeschool setting, preserve the procedure while converting classroom groups into parent-child, sibling, or invited-peer turns.

layer3_structure.cadence: Parallel English and Spanish phonics and word-study sequences each run for 30 weeks, ten units, three weeks per unit, and five days per week. The captured Reader's Workshop contributes nine 15-minilesson guides, and Reader's Theater contributes ten five-day rehearsal and performance cycles.
layer3_structure.cadenceEvidence: Each book is organized around five (5) days of instruction.
layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Phonics Day 1 introduces the week's shared text and sound-spelling or syllable focus. Day 2 rereads and writes, then enters connected text. Day 3 transfers into independent reading and writing. Day 4 rereads and writes about the text. Day 5 reviews spelling and dictation and uses cumulative assessment. Reader's Workshop minilessons model one reading move and transfer it into small-group or independent reading. Reader's Theater cycles move from introduction through modeling, role analysis, rehearsal, performance, and reflection.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: Cumulative and language-specific. English moves from short vowels and blends through digraphs, final e, vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, diphthongs, silent letters, and alternative spellings. Spanish moves from vowels and consonants through syllables and words, contextual spellings, closed syllables, clusters, diphthongs, hiatuses, triphthongs, stress, prefixes, and suffixes. Comprehension and performance recur alongside the code work.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Every week reconnects the target to shared reading, connected text, writing, rereading, reflection, spelling or dictation, and cumulative evidence. Reader's Workshop revisits texts for different comprehension purposes. Reader's Theater uses repeated oral reading toward an authentic performance.
studyRoutines: Read or listen to the shared text and notice the target sound-spelling, syllable, or reading move.
Model blending, word building, comprehension thinking, or fluent phrasing aloud.
Practice together, then transfer the move into connected or independently chosen text.
Write words or a short text response and share evidence from the reading.
Reread for accuracy, expression, comprehension, and confidence.
Use the day's observation, dictation, cumulative check, or performance reflection to choose the next support.
layer3_structure.bookAndReaderUse: Shared texts introduce weekly language patterns and themes. Decodable or connected texts carry the target into reading and writing. Reader's Workshop guides use model texts and independent reading for comprehension transfer. Reader's Theater scripts are performance sources. Homa may create original practice materials that teach the same pattern or procedure, but must not reproduce the copyrighted source text or visual identity.
layer3_structure.homeschoolAdaptation: Keep the language-specific progression and exact instructional purpose. Whole group becomes parent and child, partner talk becomes parent-child or sibling talk, small group becomes one-to-one guided reading, independent reading stays independent, and a Reader's Theater cast may include family members, peers, recorded role turns, or a parent-child two-person adaptation.
